bull.t: Recurring Franchised Revenue And Strong Cash Generation
bull.b: McDonald’s predominantly franchised model produces recurring royalties, rent, and fees tied to systemwide sales, while strong operating and free cash flow support reinvestment and obligations. Continued refranchising should further emphasize this recurring, capital-efficient earnings structure over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Very High Margins And Operating Leverage
bull.b: The company’s very high net and EBIT margins demonstrate substantial brand strength, pricing power, and operating leverage. These economics provide resilience when sales growth moderates and create capacity to fund marketing, restaurant improvements, technology, and franchisee support while preserving strong profitability.

bull.t: Global Scale, Digital Engagement, And Menu Expansion
bull.b: McDonald’s broad international footprint, share gains, loyalty engagement, and expanding beverage platform diversify growth beyond any single market. Digital sales and higher-check specialty beverages can increase frequency and average ticket, while global scale supports repeatable menu and marketing execution.

bear.t: Highly Leveraged Balance Sheet With Negative Equity
bear.b: Negative equity and very high debt leave McDonald’s with limited balance-sheet cushion if operating conditions weaken. Although cash generation can support the model, leverage raises financial risk, reduces flexibility for investment or shocks, and makes sustained execution more important over the medium term.

bear.t: Uneven U.S. Demand And Marketing Execution
bear.b: The U.S. remains the company’s most important operating market, so negative quarterly comparable sales and weaker-than-expected marketing execution could weigh on systemwide sales and franchisee economics. Planned value initiatives may help, but consistency in traffic and demand generation is not yet established.

bear.t: Higher Input Costs Could Pressure Value And Margins
bear.b: Mid-single-digit food and paper inflation would pressure restaurant-level economics and require careful pricing decisions. Passing through too much cost could weaken affordability and traffic, while absorbing it could constrain margins; the tension is material because value positioning is already a current U.S. priority.
